searchText: Hello, do we have data on how many hops do blocks pass to get to a typical node? or what's the max number of them? or p95? cc <@476250636548308992> <@498009160982724610> It's very hard to measure that. What we usually do when we estimate the number of hops is log_D (N) where N is number of nodes and D is the degree (which is 5 hops with N=10,000 and D=8) Another way to do that is to ask graph theorists what is the expected diameter of a graph with each node having degree D, but the real world graph may not look like that. Yeah I get that it's tough to measure but perhaps we can set some sentry nodes to ping at different places to try to they this? If we're at 5 hops more or less this is pretty encouraging > we can set some sentry nodes to ping at different places to try to they this I don't see how this helps. yeah, neither do I unless we modify clients to keep track of extra data off-protocol per hop. Attackers can screw up the meassurement, but there's no incentive on doing so I'm only interested in a rough estimate, doesn't need to be precise but if it were true that it's of the order of 5-10 that's great If you want me to guess, I would say 4-6. > unless we modify clients to keep track of extra data off-protocol per hop We discussed about adding this many times in the past, the only issue is when you know you connect to the original publisher, it kind of kills anonymity. yeah, it anyway is already not annonimous 🙂 we could even make it opt-in in clients... is there any way of formally proving a bound? say we're sure that with 20 we are good? (I actually think already 20 is very good for what I want to do ) I think 20 is extremly high and unlikely. Pretty sure that if it's the case there should be like <1% of the nodes that have that high number. is there any way of proving this? although I'm happy with the guess already, I can design the coding with this in mind and test it live in forced networks with more hops I have no idea 😄 5 hops would be accurate <@755590043632140352> I dont even know how you could get to 20 hops unless you have very bad peering what if we added an optional "hop count" field to the block gossip messages that clients could increment like an inverse of the IP TTL field? it could of course be "attacked" but like you said theres no incentive to do so. I'm guessing we don't want to waste a byte with this though. The main opposition to having it was that it killed anonymity and allowed us to narrow down on the message originator It would have to be non-optional to be useful for the network

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Hello, do we have data on how many hops do blocks pass to get to a typical node? or what's the max number of them? or p95?

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content: It's very hard to measure that. What we usually do when we estimate the number of hops is log_D (N) where N is number of nodes and D is the degree (which is 5 hops with N=10,000 and D=8)

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content: Another way to do that is to ask graph theorists what is the expected diameter of a graph with each node having degree D, but the real world graph may not look like that.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Yeah I get that it's tough to measure but perhaps we can set some sentry nodes to ping at different places to try to they this? If we're at 5 hops more or less this is pretty encouraging

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content:
> we can set some sentry nodes to ping at different places to try to they this
I don't see how this helps.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yeah, neither do I unless we modify clients to keep track of extra data off-protocol per hop. Attackers can screw up the meassurement, but there's no incentive on doing so

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I'm only interested in a rough estimate, doesn't need to be precise

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: but if it were true that it's of the order of 5-10 that's great

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content: If you want me to guess, I would say 4-6.

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content:
> unless we modify clients to keep track of extra data off-protocol per hop
We discussed about adding this many times in the past, the only issue is when you know you connect to the original publisher, it kind of kills anonymity.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yeah, it anyway is already not annonimous 🙂 we could even make it opt-in in clients... is there any way of formally proving a bound? say we're sure that with 20 we are good? (I actually think already 20 is very good for what I want to do )

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content: I think 20 is extremly high and unlikely. Pretty sure that if it's the case there should be like <1% of the nodes that have that high number.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: is there any way of proving this? although I'm happy with the guess already, I can design the coding with this in mind and test it live in forced networks with more hops

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content: I have no idea 😄
